head: 63d0bdf5829a0f0acab756befcc01e31b25f7653

findings.title: Status/MCP qualificam candidatos semanticamente inválidos como sólidos
findings.action: Compartilhar a recomposição completa do candidato entre check e domínio/status/MCP, incluindo notas renderizadas, fragments, policy e version_source.

findings.title: Subcheck global de release ignora corrupção do worktree
findings.action: Aplicar a mesma verificação de candidato/cópia do cut no checker, preservando a leitura histórica da tag e a distinção entre estado e integridade.

findings.title: Perda de fontes no worktree ainda vira ausência, fallback ou inventário vazio
findings.action: Provar ausência sem seguir links quebrados, inclusive ancestrais; propagar falhas de inventário. Usar fallback/default/empty somente quando a fonte estiver legitimamente ausente.

findings.title: Prepare escreve através de manifest existente e ilegível quando o link está quebrado
findings.action: Distinguir manifest inexistente de entrada existente ilegível antes de qualquer efeito; recusar o segundo sem criar o alvo do link nem reconstruir prova.

findings.title: Check preparado usa defaults sobre changelog policy inválida ou de schema futuro
findings.action: Usar um loader validante de changelog policy na qualificação/preparação; compartilhar o contrato com changelogPolicyAt, sem reinterpretar schema futuro como schema 1.

findings.title: Renderer atual invalida notas de tags históricas legítimas
findings.action: Vincular a recomposição ao contrato de renderer do cut, com tratamento explícito de legacy/unsupported sem reescrever notas ou enfraquecer detecção de adulteração.

findings.title: Recusar version_evidence.kind:null, hoje equivalente ao kind vazio do engine; source exato e value continuam obrigatórios.
Harmonizar filtros de auxiliares no archive: README é ignorado pelo loader, mas recusado pelo snapshot; a divergência é recusa excessiva.
Mostrar Snapshot.Limits no status humano e qualificar o diagnóstico de candidato em publicclaims. JSON mantém limites e o gate de publicação exige Sound.
Ampliar o pattern do check release-manifest-tag-integrity-integration para TestF*, TestR2* e TestR4*; go test ./... já executa esses testes.
Reconciliar texto de authoring da spec que diz que código/testes ainda não existem; manter o item editorial já aberto, sem duplicação.

Explicitar/harmonizar o tratamento de symlinks do worktree com bytes idênticos: ReleaseFilesGaps/archival seguem o link, LoadReleaseFragments recusa. O probe preserva todos os digests e não demonstra aceitação de conteúdo divergente; a árvore da tag já exige arquivo regular.

Fazer o smoke histórico falhar ou declarar skip se releases não puderem ser lidas ou o conjunto estiver vazio; o teste atual ignora ReadDir e pode passar com zero fixtures. Nesta revisão as 75 releases foram verificadas explicitamente.

@@ -1,5 +1,14 @@
 # POSE v1.1.0
 
+## Compatibility
+
+This release introduces 2 governance contracts. An engine older than v1.1.0 does not know them, so it never applies them: reviews it performs are judged by the rules it has.
+
+- `component-aware` — review plans are resolved per component
+  Adopting it writes `component_aware_adopted_at` at the top level of the review policy. Engines before 2.0.2 refuse a policy carrying a key they do not model, so they stop reading this repository altogether until they are updated — every tool reading it has to move together.
+- `review-bundles` — review approval is recorded against an immutable sealed bundle
+  Adopting it writes `review_bundles_adopted_at` at the top level of the review policy. Engines before 2.0.2 refuse a policy carrying a key they do not model, so they stop reading this repository altogether until they are updated — every tool reading it has to move together.
+
 ## Added
 
 - Review can now resolve a deterministic effective plan for the actual components affected by a spec, milestone or roadmap. The plan composes typed review overlays, component-specific criteria and safe native POSE tool recommendations, and binds new review attempts to both scope and plan digests.  The migration also preserves the configured exemption for completed scopes and approved attempts that predate review-policy or component-aware adoption. (pose-component-aware-review-plans)

 # POSE v2.0.0
 
+## Compatibility
+
+This release introduces a governance contract. An engine older than v2.0.0 does not know it, so it never applies it: reviews it performs are judged by the rules it has.
+
+- `evidence-vocabulary` — a passed criterion must cite evidence the sealed bundle contains, of a class the criterion asks for
+  Adopting it writes `evidence_vocabulary_reconciled_at` at the top level of the review policy. Engines before 2.0.2 refuse a policy carrying a key they do not model, so they stop reading this repository altogether until they are updated — every tool reading it has to move together.
+
 ## Added
 
 - `pose review attest` accepts `--criterion ID|disposition|evidence|rationale`, so a reviewer can record the dispositions the engine already models. Every required criterion used to become `passed` with evidence picked from the supplied refs, which was harmless while nothing checked that evidence and a dead end once a `passed` must cite sealed evidence of a demanded class: a criterion that genuinely does not apply could only be claimed as passed on evidence that does not support it, or left blocking the closeout.  `not-applicable` without a rationale is refused at the flag rather than only at sealing, and a criterion nobody names keeps the current default.  A criterion dispositioned `finding` must now name a finding the attestation records. Nothing tied the two together before: the disposition was validated and findings were only rejected when they existed and stayed open, so a criterion the reviewer explicitly did not pass reported a clean closeout. (pose-attest-records-not-applicable)
